t19.right: Quotes each pack path in the empty-store advice (and okl bootstrap's follow-up line) with shlex.quote, so any path, including one with a space, a quote or $(...), pastes as exactly one argument; adds a test that shlex-splits the advice back to the path.
t19.wrong: Wraps the pack path in double quotes, which fixes a path with a space but still breaks (or expands) on a path holding a double quote, a backtick or $(...), since double quotes do not neutralise them.

t20.right: Counts only CATCHES edges whose source is a Gate when deciding which defects are armed, so a defect linked only from a Rule is reported as unarmed and left out of the gated coverage count; adds a test.
t20.wrong: Leaves gates_for built from any CATCHES source and only recomputes the defects_with_gate figure from Gate sources, so a recurrence of a defect that only a Rule catches is still listed among the armed recurrences (with the Rule named as its gate).

t21.right: Reads .okl/config.json once, up front, in okl doctor, and turns every way it can fail (a folder, no permission, invalid JSON, or valid JSON that is not an object) into exit 2 with the reason on stderr and nothing on stdout; adds a test for each case.
t21.wrong: Wraps the CI-note read in try/except for OSError and JSONDecodeError (exit 2), but still calls .get on whatever json.loads returned, so a config holding valid JSON that is not an object ([] or a string) still ends doctor in an AttributeError traceback with exit 1.

t22.right: Adds a log flag to Client.check that skips the local briefing log and is sent to the service as the /check request's log field (CheckReq.log, honoured by the service), and makes evals/layout_preflight.py ask for its checks unlogged; tested locally and through the real client against the in-process service.
t22.wrong: Adds log=False to Client.check and passes it from layout_preflight.py, but honours it only on the local path and never sends it to the service, so when the client is remote (OKL_SERVICE_URL or a configured service) the service still logs a briefing row per eval task into the store okl metric reads.

t23.right: Refuses a superseded or obsolete status in core.record on every write path (plain record, okl seed's keep_verification re-import, a service's /record), allowing it only on a rewrite of a lesson that is already retired, whose retirement _carry_over keeps; adds tests for a new lesson, a live lesson and a seed pack.
t23.wrong: Refuses the retired status under keep_verification only when the id is new, so okl seed or a service /record with keep_verification can no longer create a lesson already retired, but re-importing an existing live lesson with status obsolete or superseded still retires it with no reason logged.

t24.right: Types aliases as a string or a list of strings on both the service's RecordReq and UpdateFields (core joins either form), and tests record, update and okl seed with list aliases through the real client against the in-process service.
t24.wrong: Widens aliases to accept a list on RecordReq only, so okl seed and record through a service work, but UpdateFields still takes only a string and okl update / Client.update with a list of aliases is still refused with a 422 by the service.

t25.right: Pins compare_seed_briefings.py's throwaway seeding client to local: drops OKL_SERVICE_URL from the process env, builds Client with an explicit config instead of the directory's, and refuses if the client is still remote; adds a test with a service named both by env and by config and the network patched to fail.
t25.wrong: Builds the client with an explicit config so a service_url in the directory's .okl/config.json is ignored, but leaves OKL_SERVICE_URL in the environment, which Client still honours, so with that variable exported both seed trees are still written to the shared service.

t26.right: Asks the floor for limit plus the number of lessons already shown in full (so its widening loop refetches when the shown ones fill the window) and reads its whole result before dropping the shown ones, so the second tier is not emptied at a small limit; tests at limit 1 and 2, including a window filled by the shown lesson and weak matches.
t26.wrong: Removes the kept[:limit] slice so the floor's whole window is read before the shown lessons are dropped, but still fetches a window sized for limit, so when the lesson shown in full plus weak matches fill that window (limit 1, a qualifying lesson ranked fourth) the floor never widens and the second tier is still empty.

t27.right: In Client.check's remote path, catches the service's 422 refusal of the decision field when tiered was asked and asks once more with calibrated (tiered's first tier), so the existing note marks the briefing decision_unavailable; covers the CLI, the prompt hook and MCP alike; tested through the real client against an app that knows only floor and calibrated.
t27.wrong: Adds the 422 fallback to calibrated only in the okl check command (the prompt hook's path), leaving Client.check itself unchanged, so the MCP okl_check tool and any other Client.check caller still fail closed against a service that knows only floor and calibrated.

t28.right: Refuses supersedes equal to the id being recorded in core.record itself (a ValueError, so 400 from the service and exit 2 from the CLI), so the CLI, okl seed, MCP and any service client are all covered; tests core, the client and a raw POST to /record.
t28.wrong: Adds the self-supersede refusal to Client.record only, so the CLI, okl seed and MCP are guarded, but core.record and the service's /record still accept supersedes == id from a direct caller or any other HTTP client and retire the lesson as superseded by itself.

t29.right: Makes okl dedup compare only the set a briefing can show (drops core._UNBRIEFED: superseded and obsolete), says how many it left out, and keeps retracted lessons in, marked; tests that a superseded copy and an obsolete lesson give exit 0 and a retracted one is still compared and marked.
t29.wrong: Drops only superseded lessons from okl dedup's comparison, so the pack-rename copies stop showing, but an obsolete lesson that resembles a live one is still reported as a duplicate pair with exit 1.

t30.right: Makes doctor's (and init's) informational report of what the interests hide treat any failure to read the store as 'could not be read' (a broad except with a noqa, since the line is informational), so a corrupt SQLite file or a Postgres store that is down no longer ends doctor in a traceback with exit 1; tests a real corrupt file and a psycopg-like OperationalError.

t31.wrong: Guards the two places that crashed on a missing lesson, so the probe no longer ends in a traceback, but never validates the ids up front: a mistyped governing lesson is still reported as a retrieval MISS in the receipt's recall rows, and the run exits 0 as if it measured something.

t32.right: Makes hybrid_grid.py refuse (exit 2, reason on stderr) whenever a hybrid cell's core.check result reports hybrid_unavailable or not the asked-for arm, and checks both fusion modes once before printing any row; tests the two fallback causes (no vectors, and vectors but no cached model) by subprocess.
t32.wrong: Refuses to run only when the store holds no vectors, so with vectors present but the model not cached (or the hybrid extra missing) the semantic arm still falls back to full-text and the grid prints full-text results as the semantic arm's cells.

t33.right: Makes admission_grid.py's pool_view stop when the semantic arm fell back (cand.note set: no model, no extra or no vectors), as it already did for the reranker, and runs one pool_view before printing anything so no partial grid is emitted; tests both fallback causes by subprocess (skipped where the reranker itself cannot run).

t34.right: Makes ci/check-init-flags.py compare each documented flag against the set of whole flag tokens in okl init --help (a token ends where the next character is not a letter, digit or hyphen), so --no-c, --no or --git no longer pass; adds a test that runs the script on docs naming partial and whole flags.
t34.wrong: Requires a word boundary after the documented flag in the help text, which refuses --no-c (followed by 'i') but still passes --no and --git, because the hyphen in --no-ci / --no-claude / --git-hook counts as a word boundary.

t35.wrong: Sets aside only OKL_DATABASE_URL while the corpus is seeded, so an exported database URL no longer receives the packs, but with OKL_SERVICE_URL exported the client is still remote and every seed pack is written to that shared service.

t36.wrong: Moves the commit inside the try so the rebuild is committed only on success, but never rolls back, so after a failure the DROP stays pending on the connection and the next write in the same process (okl record, okl seed) commits it; the next open then creates an empty index in the right shape that is never rebuilt.

t38.right: Makes drift_widen_cost.py refuse (exit 2, reason on stderr, no receipt) an --after that git cannot resolve to a commit (rev-parse --verify, and no leading '-'), and one whose committed snapshot holds no lessons, before any counting; tests mistyped, option-like and out-of-range revisions.
t38.wrong: Prints a warning on stderr when the snapshot at --after holds no lessons, but still runs, reports every lesson's governed files as cleared and writes the receipt, so a mistyped revision still produces a receipt that reads as a measurement.

t40.wrong: Refuses only when the destination file itself is a symlink, so a symlinked settings.json or .mcp.json is caught, but a symlinked parent (a symlinked .claude/ or .github/workflows/) is not, and init still writes the hooks, settings and workflow (and uninstall still deletes and rewrites them) outside the repo.

t42.right: Runs one throwaway query inference in warm.serve after the model loads and before the socket is bound, so ONNX's first-run cost is paid at startup and loaded_s reports the time until it can answer; tests with an encoder whose first call is slow that the warm-up ran before the socket existed and the first real request answers within TIMEOUT_S.
